doc.md:
The selection object for GtkTreeView

The `GtkTreeSelection` object is a helper object to manage the selection
for a `GtkTreeView` widget.  The `GtkTreeSelection` object is
automatically created when a new `GtkTreeView` widget is created, and
cannot exist independently of this widget.  The primary reason the
`GtkTreeSelection` objects exists is for cleanliness of code and API.
That is, there is no conceptual reason all these functions could not be
methods on the `GtkTreeView` widget instead of a separate function.

The `GtkTreeSelection` object is gotten from a `GtkTreeView` by calling
gtk_tree_view_get_selection().  It can be manipulated to check the
selection status of the tree, as well as select and deselect individual
rows.  Selection is done completely view side.  As a result, multiple
views of the same model can have completely different selections.
Additionally, you cannot change the selection of a row on the model that
is not currently displayed by the view without expanding its parents
first.

One of the important things to remember when monitoring the selection of
a view is that the `GtkTreeSelection`::changed signal is mostly a hint.
That is, it may only emit one signal when a range of rows is selected.
Additionally, it may on occasion emit a `GtkTreeSelection`::changed signal
when nothing has happened (mostly as a result of programmers calling
select_row on an already selected row).

count_selected_rows.brief: Returns the number of rows that have been selected in `tree`.
count_selected_rows.md: Returns the number of rows that have been selected in `tree`.

get_mode.md:
Gets the selection mode for `selection`. See
gtk_tree_selection_set_mode().

get_selected.brief: Sets `iter` to the currently selected node if `selection` is set to %GTK_SELECTION_SINGLE or %GTK_SELECTION_BROWSE.
get_selected.md:
Sets `iter` to the currently selected node if `selection` is set to
%GTK_SELECTION_SINGLE or %GTK_SELECTION_BROWSE.  `iter` may be NULL if you
just want to test if `selection` has any selected nodes.  `model` is filled
with the current model as a convenience.  This function will not work if you
use `selection` is %GTK_SELECTION_MULTIPLE.

get_selected_rows.brief: Creates a list of path of all selected rows.
get_selected_rows.md:
Creates a list of path of all selected rows. Additionally, if you are
planning on modifying the model after calling this function, you may
want to convert the returned list into a list of `GtkTreeRowReference`s.
To do this, you can use gtk_tree_row_reference_new().

To free the return value, use:

```c
g_list_free_full (list, (GDestroyNotify) gtk_tree_path_free);
```

get_tree_view.brief: Returns the tree view associated with `selection`.
get_tree_view.md: Returns the tree view associated with `selection`.

get_user_data.brief: Returns the user data for the selection function.
get_user_data.md: Returns the user data for the selection function.

iter_is_selected.brief: Returns `TRUE` if the row at `iter` is currently selected.
iter_is_selected.md: Returns `TRUE` if the row at `iter` is currently selected.

path_is_selected.brief: Returns `TRUE` if the row pointed to by `path` is currently selected.
path_is_selected.md:
Returns `TRUE` if the row pointed to by `path` is currently selected.  If `path`
does not point to a valid location, `FALSE` is returned

select_all.md:
Selects all the nodes. `selection` must be set to %GTK_SELECTION_MULTIPLE
mode.

select_range.brief: Selects a range of nodes, determined by `start_path` and `end_path` inclusive.
select_range.md:
Selects a range of nodes, determined by `start_path` and `end_path` inclusive.
`selection` must be set to %GTK_SELECTION_MULTIPLE mode.

selected_foreach.brief: Calls a function for each selected node.
selected_foreach.md:
Calls a function for each selected node. Note that you cannot modify
the tree or selection from within this function. As a result,
gtk_tree_selection_get_selected_rows() might be more useful.

set_mode.brief: Sets the selection mode of the `selection`.
set_mode.md:
Sets the selection mode of the `selection`.  If the previous type was
%GTK_SELECTION_MULTIPLE, then the anchor is kept selected, if it was
previously selected.

set_select_function.md:
Sets the selection function.

If set, this function is called before any node is selected or unselected,
giving some control over which nodes are selected. The select function
should return `TRUE` if the state of the node may be toggled, and `FALSE`
if the state of the node should be left unchanged.

unselect_range.brief: Unselects a range of nodes, determined by `start_path` and `end_path` inclusive.
unselect_range.md:
Unselects a range of nodes, determined by `start_path` and `end_path`
inclusive.

mode.brief: Selection mode. See gtk_tree_selection_set_mode() for more information on this property.
mode.md:
Selection mode.
See gtk_tree_selection_set_mode() for more information on this property.

changed.brief: Emitted whenever the selection has (possibly) changed.
changed.md:
Emitted whenever the selection has (possibly) changed. Please note that
this signal is mostly a hint.  It may only be emitted once when a range
of rows are selected, and it may occasionally be emitted when nothing
has happened.
